date_note: ASCII.jp (25 November) says JAXA confirmed the unauthorized access on 18 November and announced it on 24 November.
title: JAXA says unauthorized access to its public Earth-observation data system exposed account data of 2000 users
summary: ASCII.jp reports that JAXA announced on 24 November unauthorized access to a public information system that distributes Earth-observation data. Per that report, JAXA said attackers exploited a command injection vulnerability in part of the web application and installed a backdoor, and that account names and encrypted passwords of 2000 users were leaked. JAXA stopped the system; no resumption date. Mynavi, relaying JAXA, says no trace of access to public observation data was found.
plain: Japan's space agency JAXA says attackers got into its public Earth-observation data system and that account names and encrypted passwords of 2000 users leaked. The system is stopped.
exec: A national space agency's public data service leaked account names and encrypted passwords of 2000 users, per ASCII.jp's report of JAXA's announcement.
action: As relayed by Mynavi, JAXA says it never asks for passwords by email and urges caution with suspicious emails posing as JAXA.
